explanation: The faint band of light called the Milky Way is our galaxy's disc, seen edge-on from inside it. Our nearest large neighbour, the Andromeda Galaxy, is about 2.5 million light-years away.

claims.text: The Solar System lies inside the Milky Way galaxy.
The Andromeda, Whirlpool and Sombrero galaxies are separate galaxies beyond the Milky Way, so none of them contains the Solar System.
The band of light called the Milky Way in the night sky is the disc of our own galaxy, seen edge-on from inside it.
The Andromeda Galaxy is the nearest large galaxy to the Milky Way.
The Andromeda Galaxy is about 2.5 million light-years from Earth.
